summary: Shasta County steel lookout tower, built 1980 around a 1933 CCC-era lookout; Bear Fire evacuated it in 1990; Cal Fire Shasta-Trinity; NHLR-registered 2019.

facts.design: Plesha design (Plan No. 1548-lA) steel tower with a second-story room and 732-6A type cab; steel columns first intended for atomic bomb test towers

access.note: About 5 miles from paved road, behind locked gates, per the Register

facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection - Shasta-Trinity Unit (Cal Fire SHU)

events.note: Original CCC-era lookout (L-601 with BC-301 cab), per the Register's description. The Built field gives 1980 for the current steel tower
Older tower and cab demolished; steel tower erected around the original and finished with a second-story room and 732-6A cab
Bear Fire overran the site, forcing evacuation of the lookout station

notes_for_editor: Register is the only detailed source. Its Built field is 1980 for the current steel tower; the description places a 1933 CCC-era lookout on the same site, so both dates are kept and no correction is proposed. The brief says standing; no source dated after the 2008 list confirms the cab's current condition, so status is left at the record's value. The Cal Fire list is a 2008 document and says only that the lookout may be staffed that season; it is not evidence of current staffing. Access 'restricted' follows the Register's wording about locked gates. Not used: an ALERTCalifornia Facebook post on the lookout (fetch_text and WebFetch both returned only 'Facebook'), and a search snippet saying the lookout is no longer in service, which I could not confirm from a readable page. The Forest Lookouts Bear Mountain page had no article text beyond its index and header. No photos added; the Register lists a 1953 National Archives photo but I did not read its file. Page reads: 6 total, 1 WebSearch.
